newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH FIRM BAUMA TO ISSUE SHARES TO TWO US FUNDS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH FIRM BAUMA TO ISSUE SHARES TO TWO US FUNDS.

text.p: Shareholders of Polish construction materials maker Bauma SA will vote on March 27 on whether to issue 420,000 common shares worth 10 zlotys each to two U.S. investment funds, Bauma said on Tuesday.
The company said in a statement that the two funds were the Polish-American Enterprise Fund 1 and the Polish-American Enterprise Fund 2, which it said would be medium-term financial investors.

The two funds underwrote 300,000 shares each in Bauma's January 1.2-million-share initial public offering, also at 10 zlotys per share, in which investors subscribed for 3,903,205 shares and had their bids reduced by 69.26 percent.

Bauma, which seeks to enter the parallel market of the Warsaw bourse, has another 130,421 shares approved for public trade and another 1.2 million registered shares held by its founders not yet approved for trade.

In 1995 the company netted 418,000 zlotys on sales of 15.4 million zlotys. It expects profits to rise to 1.5 million zlotys on sales of 14 million in 1996 and to 2.1 million zlotys on sales of 19.6 million in 1997.
